title: Child care funding, tourism grants and housing transfer
subtitle: Cultural tourism grants, ROWCHI housing transfer, public art gallery funding direction, and refugee pressures on shelters.
overview: The Community and Health Services Committee recommended adding $8,380,262 to the 2023 Children's Services operating budget, fully funded by the Province, to support Canada-Wide Early Learning and Child Care implementation. This came through the consent agenda {{vote:m1}} and then a separate vote {{vote:m2}}.

The committee also recommended $163,550 in Cultural Drivers of Tourism pilot grants {{vote:m3}}, and recommended that the Region accept ownership of two community housing properties, 92 units in total, from Region of Waterloo Community Housing Inc. {{vote:m4}}. The Region would pay off the mortgage on the Cambridge property from its Housing Capital Reserve. Both items go to Council for a final decision.

The committee directed staff to report on September 12 on including public art galleries in Regional operating funding. Staff also reported a sharp rise in refugees and asylum seekers using the shelter system. A councillor's notice of motion was deferred to September so delegations can speak first. These recommendations go to Council for adoption.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended adding $8,380,262 to the 2023 Children's Services operating budget, funded fully by the Ministry of Education, for Canada-Wide Early Learning and Child Care implementation.
The committee recommended 2023 allocations of $163,550 under the Cultural Drivers of Tourism Pilot Grant Program.

The committee recommended accepting ownership of two community housing properties (92 units) at 199 Elm Ridge Drive, Kitchener and 86 Elgin St. S, Cambridge, and paying off the Elgin St. S mortgage from the Housing Capital Reserve.
The committee received the consent agenda items for information and approved them, including the child care funding update.

debate: On the tourism grants, one councillor asked whether the awards were fairly spread across cities and townships, noting fewer to Cambridge. Staff said applications came from across the region in this pilot year and that they will promote the program more widely.

Councillors asked why a cultural festival organization was not on the list. Staff said it already receives operating funding through the major arts and culture program, and the guidelines avoid funding one organization from several programs.

A councillor raised letting public art galleries apply for operating funding, which Council ruled out in 2000. After discussion, the amendment was withdrawn and the idea became direction to staff to report back in September.

On the housing transfer, a councillor asked why property was moving between Regional entities. Staff said the Region cannot hold mortgages, so a separate entity held the buildings until the debt could be dealt with. The entity will stay as a shell for future use.

On shelter pressures, staff said the settlement system is fractured across housing, health care and translation, and that coordination with settlement agencies is under way. A councillor asked about remaining hotel capacity, and staff did not have a current occupancy figure.
